5. A complete conditional FPTAS, and its missing premise

A general derandomization hypothesis does yield the full requested bit contract. Making that implication explicit is useful because it identifies a genuine sufficient operation and avoids treating randomness enumeration as free.

Hypothesis

Assume a specified uniform generator

$$G_W:\{0,1\}^{r(W)}\longrightarrow\{0,1\}^{W}$$

with known fixed computable constants $c,d,C_G$, such that

$$r(W)\le\lceil c\log_2W\rceil,
\qquad
\operatorname{Time}(G_W)\le C_GW^d,$$

and $G_W$ fools every Boolean circuit of at most $W$ gates to additive error $1/8$.

This generator is an additional premise. It has not been constructed unconditionally in this work.

Fix a bounded-time rational-bit implementation of the credited permanent FPRAS. Let $q(K)$ be its fixed computable polynomial bound on bit work and random bits, when run to relative tolerance $\epsilon/4$ and success probability at least $3/4$, where

$$K=2+n+B_A+\operatorname{bits}(\epsilon)+\lceil\epsilon^{-1}\rceil.$$

Deterministic algorithm under the hypothesis

Perform the exact zero test first. Otherwise set

$$\eta=\epsilon/4,
\qquad
W=C_0(q(K)+K)^3,$$

where the fixed computable constant $C_0$ accommodates the Boolean simulation and rational comparisons below.

Enumerate every seed of $G_W$. For each seed:

- Compute $G_W(s)$.

- Run the FPRAS using its first $q(K)$ bits as the random tape.

- Retain its rational output.

Take the exact rational median $z$ of all outputs, and return

$$\boxed{
L=\frac z{1+\eta},
\qquad
U=\frac z{1-\eta}.
}$$

Why this does not require knowing which outputs are correct

Fix $A,\epsilon$. Consider the circuit that simulates the FPRAS and tests whether its output belongs to

$$[(1-\eta)P/D,\;(1+\eta)P/D],$$

using the exact integers $P,D$ from Section 2.

For the proof, hardwire $P,D$ into this circuit. Their polynomial height makes the resulting circuit have at most $W$ gates after choosing $C_0$ appropriately. Rational comparison is performed by integer cross multiplication.

The algorithm does not receive those integers, and does not construct or call this testing circuit. The circuit exists only to apply the generator’s universal fooling guarantee.
